question_en: Which of the following is best described as a necessary characteristic for an effective financial reporting framework?
option_a: Consistency in the measurement basis used across the balance sheet
option_c: Uniform treatment of transactions bydifferent entities
explanation_en:
An effective framework should enhance the transparency of the underlying economics through
the financial statements; transparency arises through full disclosure and fair presentation.

question_en: For which of the following assets is it most appropriate to test for impairment at least annually?
option_a: A trademark with an indefinite expected life
option_b: A patent with a legal life of 20 years
option_c: Land
explanation_en:
Intangible assets with indefinite lives need to be tested for impairment at least annually.
Property, plant, and equipment (including land) and intangibles with finite lives are only tested
if there has been a significant change or other indication of impairment.

question_en: In a period of rising prices, when compared with a company that uses weighted average cost for inventory, a company using FIFO will most likely report higher values for its:
option_c: inventory turnover.
explanation_en:
In periods of rising prices, FIFO results in a higher inventory value and a lower cost of goods
sold and thus a higher net income. The higher net income increases return on sales. The higher
reported net income also increases retained earnings and thus results in a lower debt-to-equity
ratio, not a higher one. The combination of higher inventory and lower cost of goods sold (CGS)
decreases inventory turnover (CGS/Inventory).

question_en: The following excerpt was taken from the notes of a company's financial statements that were prepared in accordance with International Financial Reporting Standards. All figures are in thousands of Australian dollars. The note leads an analyst to believe that the rapid reversal of the impairment loss related to the broadcast licensesarose as an attempt by management to manage earnings. If the analyst's belief is correct, her analysis of the original 2013 financial statements would most likely have shown that, compared with the economic reality in 2013, the company had:
option_c: overstated net profit margin.
explanation_en:
The broadcast licenses were written down in 2012, but the write-down was reversed in 2014.
Therefore, during 2013 the intangible assets were understated, which would have understated
amortization expense for the year and increased profit. Thus, in 2013 net profit margin was
overstated.

option_c: estimates ofwarranty expense.
explanation_en:
Net revenue means that the revenue number is reported after adjustments for cash or volume
discounts or for estimatedreturns.

question_en: Analysts can best address the challenges of comparing financial statements prepared under US GAAP with those prepared under International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) by:
option_a: monitoring changes in both sets of standards and interpreting cautiously.
option_b: assuming differences are minor given US GAAP and IFRS convergence.
option_c: referring to the reconciliation from IFRS to US GAAP provided in the notes.
explanation_en:
Significant differences still exist between IFRS and US GAAP, and in most cases, analysts will
lack the information necessary to makes specific adjustments to address these differences. As
such, comparisons must be interpretedcautiously.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\7. EXTRA QB-700MCQs\EXTRA 700 MCQs.pdf
question_en: To evaluate the potential effect of an innovative and unique type of business transaction on financial statements, an analyst's best approach is to:
option_a: gain an understanding of the transaction's economic purpose.
option_b: consider the approach taken for "new" transactions that arose in the past.
option_c: monitor the actions of standard setters and regulators.
explanation_en:
By understanding the economic purpose of a transaction and applying the conceptual
framework, an analyst may be able to evaluate the potential effect on financial statements, even
in the absence of specific standards.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\7. EXTRA QB-700MCQs\EXTRA 700 MCQs.pdf
question_en: Operating segments are most likely reportable if they constitute 10% or more of the total for all operating segments of which financial metrics?
option_c: Assets, profit/loss, or revenue
explanation_en:
A company must disclose separate information about any operating segment that constitutes
10% or more of the combined operating segments' revenue, assets, or operating profit/loss.

question_en: Which of the following is least likely to be an acceptable approach for accounting standard setting bodies to use when developing accounting standards?
option_c: Revenue/expense-based
explanation_en:
The revenue/expense-based approach is a measurement approach, not a standard setting
approach.

question_en: Compared with the management discussion and analysis (MD&A), notes to the financial statements are the most appropriate source for:
option_a: aspects of accounting policy choices most important to understanding the financial statements.
option_b: information on capital expenditures and how they support the entity's strategic direction.
option_c: a comprehensive description of allof the entity's accounting policy choices. 56
explanation_en:
The notes provide a comprehensive description of all of the entity's accounting policies,
irrespective of whether judgment was required or whether the policies are important in
understanding the financial statements.

question_en: If a company capitalizes an expenditure related to capital assets instead of expensing it, ignoring taxes, the company will most likely report:
option_a: the same free cash flow to the firm (FCFF) in that period.
option_b: a lower cash flow per share in that period.
option_c: ahigher earnings per share in future periods.
explanation_en:
The FCFF [Cash flow from operations (CFO) + Interest × (1-t)-Capital expenditures] would be
the same. CFO and capital expenditures would both increase by the same amount (ignoring
taxes). Therefore, net effect on FCFF would be zero.

question_en: For a company that prepares its financial statements under IFRS, for which of the following assets is it most likely that itcould report using the fair value model?
option_a: A building owned by the company and leased out to tenants
option_b: Houses built by the company for sale to customers
option_c: A building the company owns and uses to house its administrative activities
explanation_en: Under IFRS a building owned for the purpose of earning rentals or capital appreciation–in this case the one owned by the company and leased out to tenants - is an investment property and can be reported under either the cost model or fair value model.

question_en: Along withrelevance, the most critical qualitative characteristic of financial information is:
option_c: understandability.
explanation_en:
According to the conceptual frameworks adopted under both International Financial Reporting
Standards and US GAAP, faithful representation and relevance are the two fundamental
qualitative characteristics that make financial information useful.

question_en: The best description of a classified statement of financial position is one that:
option_a: distinguishes between current and non-current assets and liabilities.
option_b: is supported by note disclosures relevant to understanding its components.
option_c: has not been audited.
explanation_en:
Classified statements of financial position distinguish between current and non-current assets
and liabilities. Classified statements are required under International Financial Reporting
Standards unless a liquidity-based presentation provides more relevant and reliable
information.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\7. EXTRA QB-700MCQs\EXTRA 700 MCQs.pdf
question_en: The objective of general purpose financial reporting is bestdescribed as:
option_a: facilitating resource allocation decisions by current and potential investors and creditors.
option_b: reporting an entity's economic resources and claims, and changes therein, to shareholders.
option_c: providing information about financial performance to a wide range of users.
explanation_en:
According to the Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting 2010 within the International
Financial Reporting Standards, as well as Concept Statement 8 under US GAAP, "the objective
of general purpose financial reporting is to provide financial information about the reporting
entity that is useful to existing and potential investors, lenders, and other creditors in making
decisions about providing resources to the entity."
